title: How a JFET Works Explained Simply | PUC Electronics Class 12
description:
Aarav opens a broken earphone mic. Its signal is so weak it can barely push any current, yet a tiny part inside reads it without taking current from it: a field effect transistor. We start with a garden hose (squeeze it and less water flows, while your hand takes no water), then build an n channel JFET piece by piece: the n type channel, the source and the drain, the two p type gate regions and their p n junctions, and the n channel and p channel symbols.

On a live breadboard the gate goes from 0 V to -1 V, -2 V and -4 V: the grey depletion layers grow, the channel narrows, the electrons slow down and the oscilloscope shows the drain current stepping down to zero at V_GS(off), while the gate current stays near zero. Then the working in five small steps (reverse biased gate, wider depletion layers, R = rho L / A, less drain current, pinch-off), unipolar versus bipolar, a worked example on the huge input resistance of the gate, the exam trap (the gate junction is always reverse biased), where it is asked, an original practice question with a full solution, and a formula card to screenshot.

This is Episode 62 of PUC Electronics, Class 12, Chapter 1: Field Effect Transistor (FET) (Karnataka II PUC Electronics). The FET is not in the rationalised NCERT/CBSE Class 12 Physics book or the ISC Physics syllabus, so this lesson follows the Karnataka PUC Electronics syllabus.

In this video:
